model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity on tangible book (engine route; residual-income equivalent: GAAP earnings after regulatory capital retention, preferred stock deducted in the equity bridge, net debt zero)

equity_bridge.note: us-gaap:PreferredStockValue $2,500m at 30 Jun 2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q), unchanged since 2023; dividends $143m/yr (H1 2026 $72m). Deducted at book because the flows are total net income before preferred dividends.

historical_growth.fcf_series_note: For a bank the distributable-earnings series is GAAP net income (already after share-based compensation): FY2020 1,343 (COVID CECL build); FY2021 2,625 (reserve release, PPP fees - the peak); FY2022 1,917; FY2023 967 (deposit repricing, FDIC special assessment); FY2024 -161 (Q3-Q4 2024 securities repositioning losses of ~$900m after-tax funded by the Scotiabank capital); FY2025 1,829 (SEC XBRL NetIncomeLoss). The 5-year CAGR (6.4%) runs FY2020 trough to FY2025; the 3-year (-1.6%) runs from the FY2022 NIM peak. Revenue = NII + noninterest income (GAAP): FY2020 6,715; FY2022 7,272; FY2023 6,413; FY2024 4,619 (repositioning losses inside noninterest income; underlying ~6.0bn); FY2025 7,478. Diluted EPS FY2020 1.28, FY2022 1.94, FY2025 1.52 (share count up 19% on the Scotiabank issuance).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case 10-year average revenue growth (6.0% FY27 tapering to 2.5%), anchored on FY2026-27 guidance (NII +9-11% FY26, NIM tailwinds through 2027) rather than the 0.9-2.2% historical revenue CAGRs, which span the 2022-24 rate-shock trough and the FY2024 repositioning loss. Equity CAGRs are distorted by the $2.8bn Scotiabank issuance and AOCI swings.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-year CAGR (14.9%) diverges >30% from revenue (0.9%) and EPS (-7.8%): book value grew through the $2.8bn Scotiabank share issuance (Aug-Dec 2024, ~163m shares) and the $4.3bn AOCI recovery from Sep 2023, not through retained earnings, so equity CAGR does not describe per-share earnings power. EPS 3-year is negative because FY2022 was the NIM peak, FY2023-24 carried deposit repricing and the repositioning loss, and the share count rose 19%. Growth is taken from the guidance and the revenue path.

scenario_narratives.base: KeyCorp delivers the guided NIM recovery - exit-2026 NIM of 3.00-3.05% and the remaining ~$9bn of low-yield fixed-rate assets repricing through 2027 - on 4-5% loan growth, with fees compounding mid-single digits on KeyBanc Capital Markets, wealth and Clearwater UK. Expenses grow ~3.5% so the GAAP efficiency ratio improves from ~61% to ~58% and then stalls, because KeyCorp has never sustained a PNC-class cost base. Provisions normalise to ~45bp mid-cycle. GAAP EPS reaches ~$2.07 in FY2027 and ~$2.55 by FY2031; 66-83% of earnings are distributed once the AOCI-accretion surplus has been returned. At a 10.5% cost of equity and a ~14.5% return on tangible common equity the franchise is worth ~1.5x tangible book - which is what the market pays today.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Fed holds, the curve steepens and NIM exits 2027 above 3.20%; commercial loans grow 8-10% for a second year on deposit share gains; a multi-year M&A upcycle lifts KeyBanc/Clearwater fees 10% a year and Scotiabank cross-border referrals start to show. Positive operating leverage takes efficiency to 56% by FY2030, credit stays benign, ROTCE reaches 16-17%, FY2028 EPS clears $2.45 and the buyback runs at the full $3.0bn authorisation. The market's 9.9x forward multiple re-rates toward the 11-12x regional-bank norm.
scenario_narratives.bear: The repricing tailwind is blunted: the Fed cuts fast into a slowdown so reinvestment yields fall while deposit costs stay sticky, NIM plateaus near 2.95%, capital-markets fees drop ~20%, and loan growth stops. A mid-sized credit cycle (CRE, agriculture and consumer-goods-linked commercial exposures management already flags) pushes provisions to ~85bp in FY2028. With no operating leverage the efficiency ratio stays in the low 60s, ROTCE settles at ~10-11% - barely above the cost of equity - and the buyback is halted to hold marked CET1 above 9.5%. EPS falls to ~$1.35 before recovering slowly.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A regional bank is valued on what it can distribute after funding its regulatory capital, discounted at a USD cost of equity - never on statutory operating cash flow (which is loan and deposit movement) and never with deposits or wholesale funding treated as net debt. GAAP net income is the flow; capital retention at NPAT x g/ROTE is the reinvestment; preferred stock is deducted at book so the common claim is valued; 10.5% is the return an owner requires from a NIM-geared US super-regional after March 2023. The result is the residual-income answer in FCFE form: at a ~14.5% return on tangible common equity and 2.5% growth the franchise is worth ~1.5x tangible book, and the 1.50x TBV / 9.9x FY2027E EPS the market pays is that base case, with neither a margin of safety nor a premium embedded.
key_risks_to_valuation: Net interest margin: 5bp on ~$170bn of average earning assets is ~$85m of NII (~1.1% of revenue, ~4% of NPAT); the base assumes the guided 3.00-3.05% exit NIM and further 2027 repricing gains, and the bear case removes most of it
Credit cycle: every 10bp on the provision rate over ~$110bn of loans is ~$110m pre-tax (~4% of NPAT); CRE, agriculture and consumer-goods-linked commercial books are management's own watch categories
Capital-markets fees: investment banking and debt placement (~12% of revenue) fell ~25% peak-to-trough in 2022-23; a 20% decline is ~$190m of revenue (~7% of NPAT) with little cost offset
Operating leverage: the base assumes GAAP efficiency improves from ~61% to 58%; every 1pp is ~$85m pre-tax (~3% of NPAT), and KeyCorp's history is a ratio in the low-to-mid 60s
Share count: the ~12m further Q3 2026 repurchase estimate and the ~9m dilutive-award count are approximations until the Q3 10-Q cover prints; each 20m shares is ~2% of value per share

Capital: marked CET1 ~9.8% is at the bottom of the 9.5-10% range; the surplus funding the $3.0bn buyback is AOCI accretion, which reverses if long rates rise, and a Basel III endgame re-proposal could change the RWA base either way

Scotiabank's 14.9% stake: a standstill-governed strategic holder is a stabiliser today, but any change in Scotiabank's intent (sale, or a bid) would reprice the shares in either direction outside this model

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NYSE regular close); 52-week range 16.47-24.07.
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 0000091576) for FY2020-FY2025 annual NII, noninterest income, noninterest expense, provision, pre-tax income, tax, net income, preferred dividends, diluted EPS, equity, goodwill, intangibles, AOCI, preferred stock, deposits, long-term debt, share-based compensation and share counts; Q2 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-08-04) facts for the 30 Jun 2026 balance sheet, Q2/H1 2026 income statement, diluted shares and the 31 Jul 2026 cover-page share count; KEY_Metrics.csv / KEY.duckdb (101 periods) for the reported history and kpis (buybacks to FY2023, cash taxes). The CSV FreeCashFlow column is statutory OCF less capex and was not used.
data_sources.qualitative: KEY_Analysis.json (2026-09-29): FY2026 guidance (revenue +7-8%, NII +9-11%, exit NIM 3.00-3.05%, loans +4-5%, NCOs 40-45bp, buybacks >= $1.3bn, CET1 9.5-10% marked target), Q1/Q2 2026 results, the $3.0bn repurchase authorisation, Scotiabank's 14.9% investment, the Clearwater UK acquisition (Aug 2026), competitive position, CRE and rate risks, bull/bear cases.

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E total revenue = net interest income + noninterest income (GAAP, not taxable-equivalent). FY2026 ends 31 Dec 2026 and is unreported; FY0 = H1 2026 actual 3,901 (NII 2,472 + noninterest income 1,429, Q2 2026 10-Q) + H2 2026 ~4,100 (Q2 run-rate was 1,956 = NII 1,250 + fees 706; NII guided +9-11% on FY2025 4,636 = ~5,050-5,150 with NIM rising from 2.89% in Q2 to a 3.00-3.05% exit rate; fees ~755/quarter on the investment-banking pipeline and a first full quarter of Clearwater UK). Cross-check: guidance of ~7-8% taxable-equivalent revenue growth on FY2025 7,478 GAAP = 8,000-8,075. Using FY2026E as FY0 puts year 1 = FY2027 one year from the valuation date, as the engine's end-of-year discounting requires. The CSV Revenue column (FY2025 7,513) is within 0.5% of NII + fees and is the taxable-equivalent figure; the GAAP components are used here.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,067.1m common shares outstanding at 31 Jul 2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q cover, dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding 1,067,128,554) PLUS ~9m dilutive awards (Q2 2026 diluted weighted average 1,080.0m vs basic 1,071.2m) LESS an ESTIMATED ~12m further Q3 2026 repurchases beyond the cover date (~$250m at ~$21, the pace implied by 'at least $1.3bn' for FY2026 against ~$540m spent in H1: $341m in Q2 per the Analysis, ~$200m in Q1 implied by the Feb-May cover-count decline) = ~1,064m fully diluted at the valuation date. Held FLAT thereafter: share-based compensation ($64m H1 2026) is expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count; the buyback is a distribution of the FCFE the model capitalises, not a separate driver. Scotiabank's ~163m shares (14.9%, Dec 2024) are in the base count. REFRESH from the Q3 2026 10-Q cover (due late Oct/early Nov 2026).
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction. KeyCorp is a Fed/OCC-regulated bank holding company: long-term debt $10,967m at 30 Jun 2026 and deposits $153,089m are operating funding whose cost is already inside net interest income; cash and due from banks is held against that funding and is not surplus (the CSV carries no cash figure, and none is needed). The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (net income less capital retained to fund risk-weighted-asset growth at the 9.5-10% marked CET1 target) at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added. total_debt is recorded for audit only. Preferred stock ($2,500m, ~$143m/yr of dividends) is a claim senior to common and is deducted at book in equity_bridge; the flows are therefore total net income (before preferred dividends), NOT net income to common, so the preferred cost is charged exactly once.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE = GAAP net income ~2,135 (H1 2026 actual 1,031; H2 at ~550/quarter = (2,050 revenue - ~1,235 noninterest expense - ~115 provision) x (1 - 21%)) LESS capital retained ~675 (~4.5% RWA growth x ~$15bn of marked CET1 capital, i.e. NPAT x g/ROTE). Cross-check on distributions: FY2026 common dividends ~$880m ($0.82 x ~1,075m) + buybacks >= $1,300m = ~$2.2bn, i.e. ~100% of GAAP NI distributed - funded by the ~1.4pp of CET1 above the 10% target on the unmarked basis (11.4% at Q1 2026) as AOCI accretes back; that surplus is not added to value here because it is capital currently earning the low securities yield the NII repricing tailwind already credits. reported_fcf = FCFE + share-based compensation so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory operating cash flow (FY2025 2,208; FY2022 4,469; Q1 2026 -62) is loan/deposit/trading movement and is meaningless as free cash flow for a bank; the CSV FreeCashFlow column is NOT used. reported_fcf here is the FCFE proxy before the SBC charge.
inputs.sbc_source: us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation cash-flow add-back: H1 2026 $64m (Q2 2026 10-Q) -> ~$128m FY2026E; FY2025 $132m (10-K), FY2024 $104m, FY2023 $121m (CSV StockBasedComp). ~1.6% of revenue, so the house/street band is narrow. No separate net-share-settlement tax line is tagged; taxes withheld on vesting are immaterial relative to SBC.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income ($9.0bn gross, $4.6bn net in FY2025) IS the banking business, and no cash is added to equity value (matching-asset rule satisfied in the other direction).
inputs.buyback_note: $341m repurchased in Q2 2026 (Analysis, Q2 2026 release); PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock is not tagged in XBRL after FY2023, and Q1 2026 is estimated at ~$200m from the cover-count decline. FY2026 programme 'at least $1.3bn' under the $3.0bn authorisation expanded in April 2026. FY2022-FY2024 repurchases were nil (AOCI/CET1 rebuild after the 2022-23 rate shock, then the Scotiabank recapitalisation). The flat share count is a modelling convention funded by the SBC charge in the flows; buybacks are a use of the FCFE capitalised, not an extra source of value.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-07-31 (Q2 2026 10-Q cover count, plus dilutive awards, less estimated further Q3 2026 repurchases)
inputs.book_value_anchor: Shareholders' equity $19,798m at 30 Jun 2026 less goodwill $2,752m, other intangibles $3m and preferred stock $2,500m = tangible common equity ~$14,543m = ~$13.63/share on 1,067.1m. AOCI -$2,354m (down from -$6,639m at Sep 2023 after the Q3 2024 securities repositioning that produced the FY2024 GAAP loss of -$161m) is already inside equity and accretes back as the low-coupon securities mature. TCE ratio 7.6% on $191.3bn of assets; CET1 11.4% (Q1 2026, unmarked), ~9.8% marked, vs the 9.5-10% marked operating target. Goodwill is only 14% of equity (no recent acquisitions of scale), so unlike HBAN the GAAP and tangible bases are close; ROTCE on H1 2026 annualised NI to common (~1,918) over ~$14.5bn TCE is ~13%.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in USD, the currency of the flows: 10-year US Treasury ~4.5% (late September 2026) + beta 1.2 x US equity risk premium 5.0% = 10.5%, the same rate the house used for HBAN (2026-09-29). Beta 1.2 is the measured five-year range (1.1-1.3) for a US super-regional; KeyCorp was among the more pressured regionals in March 2023 (AOCI at -$6.6bn, marked CET1 near 6%) but has since been recapitalised by Scotiabank and de-risked, so no premium over the peer rate is stacked. One rate across all three scenarios; rate-path, credit-cycle and capital-markets risk is charged in the bear flows and the 20% bear weight, not as a discount-rate premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (940 branches) are immaterial relative to $19.8bn of equity; lease cost sits inside noninterest expense and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin. No lease line and no lease liability deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interests. Preferred stock (Series D-H) is the only senior equity claim and is deducted at $2,500m liquidation value in equity_bridge (see funding_note), so the 21.0% cash-tax-rate driver is pure income tax (FY2025 effective 20.7%; H1 2026 21.1%; FY2024 was a benefit on the repositioning loss).
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity on tangible book, run through the component engine (house precedent HBAN 2026-09-29, NAB.AX 2026-09-24, IAG.AX, GL). SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book; FCFE with retention = NPAT x g/ROTE is the clean-surplus equivalent (FCFE = NPAT x (1 - g/ROTE)), and it goes through the validated slider engine, which also produces the workbook. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY entry, no prior DCF). An owner-FCF DCF on statutory cash flow is NOT used: KeyCorp's operating cash flow is loan/deposit movement and its long-term debt is operating funding, not net debt. Engine mapping: revenue = NII + noninterest income (GAAP); ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax income (revenue - noninterest expense - provision for credit losses) PLUS share-based compensation, as % of revenue (H1 2026 actual: 3,901 - 2,398 - 198 = 1,305 = 33.5% + 1.6% SBC = 35.1%; FY2025: 7,478 - 4,703 - 471 = 2,304 = 30.8% + 1.8% = 32.6%; FY2026E: 8,000 - 4,870 - 430 = 2,700 = 33.8% + 1.6% = 35.4%); sbc_pct_path = 1.6%; da_pct = 0 (depreciation and software amortisation, ~$90m/yr, are inside noninterest expense and are genuine costs for a bank, not add-backs); capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED to fund RWA growth at the ~10% marked CET1 target = NPAT margin x balance-sheet growth / return on tangible equity; cash_tax_rate_path = 21.0% income tax; wacc = cost of equity 10.5%; net_debt = 0; equity_bridge = -2,500 preferred stock. FY2027 base reconciliation: 8,000 x 1.06 = 8,480 revenue x (36.7% - 1.6%) x (1 - 21%) = 2,351 GAAP net income, less 143 preferred dividends = 2,208 to common / 1,064m = ~$2.07 GAAP EPS (FY2025 actual $1.52; H1 2026 $0.88; trailing-twelve-month $1.71), i.e. ~17% EPS growth on FY2026E ~$1.85 from the NIM tailwind, positive operating leverage and the buyback. Base ROTCE ~14.5% on ~$15.2bn TCE. Residual-income cross-check on tangible book: P/TBV = (ROTCE - g)/(CoE - g) = (14.5 - 2.5)/(10.5 - 2.5) = 1.50x x $13.63 = ~$20.4/share, which the engine base should approximate; the market's 1.50x TBV (9.9x FY2027E EPS) is therefore pricing roughly the base case. Price is the NYSE regular close on 28 Sep 2026, not an after-hours print. Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep) is unreported; 30 Jun 2026 is the latest balance sheet. All XBRL facts are from the SEC companyfacts API (CIK 0000091576), which had ingested the Q2 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-08-04) on 2026-09-29. Clearwater Corporate Finance LLP (closed Aug 2026) is an advisory boutique of undisclosed, immaterial consideration; its revenue is inside the FY2026E fee run-rate and no bridge item is carried.

bear.growth_rationale: The NIM recovery stalls: the Fed cuts faster than expected into a slowdown so the reinvestment yield on the repricing assets falls while deposit costs stay sticky, NIM plateaus at ~2.95% instead of expanding; investment-banking fees fall ~20% in a capital-markets downturn (the most cyclical fee line, ~12% of revenue); loan growth stops as commercial clients de-lever. Revenue +1% FY27, flat FY28, then 2-2.5% nominal.
bear.margin_rationale: FY27: efficiency 62.5% (revenue shortfall against a fixed cost base; FY2023 was 73.8% on the trough) - provision 8.0% (~55bp: CRE, agriculture and consumer-goods-linked commercial books management already flags as watch categories) + 1.6 = 31.1. FY28 credit cycle: provision 12.0% (~85bp; FY2020 was 1,021 = 15.2% of revenue, so this is a mid-sized cycle, not a crisis) with efficiency 63.0%: 26.6. Recovers to provision 8.0% and efficiency 62.0%: 31.6; then provision 7.0%, efficiency 61.0%: 33.6, held - no operating leverage, the efficiency ratio stays in KeyCorp's historical low-60s. FY27 GAAP EPS ~$1.65, FY28 ~$1.35; ROTCE ~10-11%, barely above the cost of equity.
bear.capex_rationale: Retention = NPAT margin ~25% x g / ROTE ~10.5% = ~2.4 x g; FY27-29 held at 5.5% despite 0-2% growth because RWA migration and reserve build in a downturn consume capital the model must top up (marked CET1 ~9.8% is at the bottom of the 9.5-10% target range, so the 2023 precedent - a buyback halt, not a raise - repeats). Terminal 2% growth retains 4.8%.

base.growth_rationale: Total revenue. FY27 6.0%: full-year effect of the 3.00-3.05% Q4 2026 exit NIM against a ~2.95% FY26 average plus the remaining ~$9bn of low-yield fixed-rate assets repricing at ~1.25pts (management: NIM tailwinds continue through 2027) gives NII +6-7%; average loans +4-5% (commercial +8-10% guided for FY26 with consumer running off); fees +5% (KeyBanc Capital Markets pipeline, record AUM in wealth, first full year of Clearwater UK). Tapers to 2.5% terminal (nominal GDP less structural deposit-beta creep) once the repricing tailwind is exhausted by FY28.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax income + SBC on revenue. FY27 36.7% = 100 - GAAP efficiency 59.4% (FY26E ~60.9% = 4,870/8,000; expenses +3.5% against revenue +6% is the positive operating leverage management has delivered in 2025-26) - provision 5.5% (~40bp NCO on ~$112bn loans + reserve build for growth; FY26E 430 = 5.4%; H1 2026 ran 198 = 5.1% with releases) + SBC 1.6. Mature 37.6% = efficiency 58.0% (KeyCorp's structural efficiency is mid-to-high 50s at best - it has never sustained PNC's low-60s adjusted ratio at scale, so no further step-down) - provision 6.0% (mid-cycle ~45bp incl. builds; FY2025 6.3%, FY2019 7.0%, FY2018 3.8%) + 1.6. FY2025 actual was 32.6%; the path assumes the guided NIM recovery and expense discipline land.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to hold marked CET1 at ~10% as RWA grows = NPAT margin (~27.7-28.4% of revenue) x balance-sheet growth / ROTE ~14.5% (total NI over TCE + preferred ~$17.5bn) = ~1.9 x g. FY27 at 5% RWA growth: 9.5% of revenue (~$805m, 34% of NPAT retained -> 66% distributed = $0.82 dividend ~$875m + ~$675m buybacks; the FY26 programme is larger because it is also returning the AOCI-accretion surplus). Steps down with balance-sheet growth (4.5% FY28, 4% FY29-30, 3.5%, 3%, 2.5% terminal) to 4.7% (~17% retained -> 83% distributed). Cross-check on CET1: 5% RWA growth on ~$15bn of marked CET1 capital needs ~$750m.

bull.growth_rationale: The Fed holds and the curve steepens, so the repricing tailwind lands at the top of the range and NIM exits 2027 above 3.20%; commercial loan growth runs 8-10% for a second year with deposit share gains funding it; KeyBanc Capital Markets and Clearwater ride a multi-year M&A upcycle with fees +10%; Scotiabank cross-border referrals begin to show. Revenue +8% FY27 fading to 3% terminal.
bull.margin_rationale: FY27: efficiency 58.5% (revenue +8% on expenses +3.5%) - provision 5.0% + 1.6 = 38.1. Positive operating leverage takes GAAP efficiency to 56.0% by FY30 with credit benign at ~5.0% of revenue (~38bp): 100 - 56.0 - 5.0 + 1.6 = 40.6, held. FY27 GAAP EPS ~$2.20, FY28 ~$2.45; ROTCE ~16-17%.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention = NPAT margin ~30.8% x g / ROTE ~16% = ~1.9 x g: higher growth needs more capital even at a better return. FY27-28 at 6% RWA growth retains 11.6% of revenue (~38% of NPAT); terminal 3% growth retains 5.8% (~19%).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 20%: KeyCorp's earnings are the most NIM-geared of the super-regional peer set (the repricing story is ~two-thirds of the guided growth), ~12% of revenue is cyclical investment-banking fees, and marked CET1 at ~9.8% sits at the bottom of the target range so a credit cycle means a buyback halt. Not 25% as for HBAN: guidance was raised twice in 2026 rather than cut, charge-offs are running at the low end, there is no acquisition integration, and CET1 on the unmarked basis (11.4%) carries a real buffer. Bull cut to 30%: it needs a Fed hold, a second year of 8-10% commercial loan growth, an M&A upcycle and an efficiency ratio KeyCorp has never sustained, all together; the base already credits the guided NIM recovery.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
